label: text
text: Canton's capture of Xochow has been confirmed now by sources which---may ---be described as "strictly anti-Red."

label: text
text: Yochow is in the northern part of Hunan province, on that part of the Hankow-Canton Railway which runs to Changsha. (Note: the southern part of the railway runs from Canton to Shiukwan, and the middle section of the line is only "projected.")

label: text
text: In their present position, the southern Nationalists may launch an early attack on Hupeh province and the strongholds of Han-kow. "Wuchang, and the Hanyang arsenal.

label: text

label: text
text: The local Portuguese community sustained a loss to day in the death of Mr. Walter Henry Wilde Loureiro, aged 56, eldest son of the late Pedro Loureiro and of Mrs. Jessie Wilde Novaes, Lisbon.

label: text
text: Death took place at the Frenc Hospital.

label: text
text: The funeral takes place this afternoon, passing the Monument at 5.30.

label: text
text: The late Mr. Loureiro had been engaged in shipping locally for many years and his long association with Hongkong was only broken during the War period when he was engaged in transport service in the Persian Gulf. At the time of his death he was Chief Engineer of the Kwangtung Steamship Company.

Weather prospects for the week-end sporting fixtures appear gloomy. The forecast till noon to-morrow is south winds, moderate; overcast, occasional rain.

label: text
text: The Observatory in the forenoon report states that pressure has decreased considerably from Vladivostok to Hakodate and slightly over central Japan and S.W. China. label: paragraph_title
text: FOUND IN MARINE DEALER'S SHOP.

label: text
text: TWO MEN CONVICTED:

label: text
text: Acting on information received by the police, two Chinese were arrested and charged before Major C. "Willson at the Central Magistracy this morning with the theft of telegraph cable in the Albany nullah between the filter beds and May Road. They both pleaded not guilty.

label: text
text: Altogether 600 feet of cable, valued at $400, the property of the Eastern Extension Telegraph Company, disappeared between August 16 and 24, as stated in a report to the police.

label: text
text: Det-Sergeant Flaherty said that when he caught the two defendants, they took the police to a marine dealer where a part of the missing cable (between 300 to 400 feet) was found; but only the lead covering. It was discovered that the defendants had sold the lead at the rate of 15 cents and three cash per catty, realising a total sum of about $40.

label: text
text: Mr. C. W. Somers, of the Eastern Extension Telegraph Company, remarked that it was hardly possible to offer for sale

label: text
text: Questioned on this point, the dealer said "he believed the defendants' statement that they bought the lead from another dealer in the street:

label: text
text: Defendants were sentenced to two months' hard labour. His Worship deferred his decision as regards the disposal of the material found.

label: paragraph_title
text: DR. KOCH'S WARNING.

label: paragraph_title
text: Govt. "Taking Necessary Steps."

label: paragraph_title
text: ASSURANCE GIVEN.

label: text
text: Object Achieved"; Resolution Withdrawn

label: text
text: Speaking of yesterday's Council meeting against the Hon. Dr. Koch's resolution for the appointment of a Committee to make investigation and report on possible measures for preventing such considerable rainstorm damage as was experienced recently, the Hon. Mr. H. W. Bird said that he did not think "that any of the damage caused by the recent storm could have been foreseen and guarded against. Taking the case of the rock which demolished the No. 3 pumping station anyone examining it would have thought that its weight alone would have prevented any power except that of an earthquake from moving it.

label: text
text: The vulnerable parts of the Colony extended throughout the whole North side, said Mr. Bird, and to examine all the works above Conduit Road and decide which were dangerous would need not only the agility of a mountain goat but the possession of second sight in an advanced degree.

label: text
text: The Director of Public Works, after stating that the instance of the boulder constituting a danger to a house,'(referred to by Dr. Koch) and the alleged reply of the P.W.D. was unknown to him, said that extensive investigations were being made and data collected with regard to retaining walls which were being kept under close observation to ascertain if in any case movement was taking place.

label: text
text: Regarding Crown Tand sold for building purposes every care would be taken in future that such was reasonably easy of development without being a danger to adjoining property. The Government could not accept responsibility for work on private buildings but must continue to restrict its operations to periodical inspections of work in progress to see that there was no departure from the approved plans and to take action in all cases where defective workmanship was discovered.

label: text
text: Emphasising that prompt consideration was always given to any report from the public with regard to dangerous conditions of the hill side and that such reports were always appreciated, the D.P.W. said that in many cases the danger only arises in the course of a few hours and is caused by the diversion of a heavy flow of water from a water course or nullah which may itself have become blocked by small boulders following exceptional rain, and however expert an officer may be this is a danger it is impossible to guard against.

label: text
text: Dr. Koch Replies.

label: text
text: In replying to the remarks of Mr. Bird and the D.P.W., Dr. Koch said that he was not in a position to give the name of the architect who had furnished him with particulars of the hillside boulder which had constituted a danger but he would endeavour to get his permission to give the locality.

label: text
text: Mr. Bird, said Dr. Koch, had only begged the question and had merely stated what they all knew. He (the speaker), knew they were not like conics to skip about from rock to rock but human beings could see where the dangerous rocks were and it did not take pre-vision of double-magnifying power to see, where they were. They were patent, they called out to one.

label: text
text: It was evident that these boulders were on disintegrated soil and when there were series of heavy rains for thirty or forty days they soaked through the rotten soil and then when another heavy rain came the rocks slipped down.

label: text
text:
Danger to University.
It was a mercy that the rock which destroyed No. 3 Pumping Station did not take another angle and destroy part of the University. If some part of the University had been damaged a little more might have been made of it than only over five coolies being killed.

text: NO DREDGER.

label: paragraph_title
text:
WHY CONSTRUCTION IS
NECESSARY.

label: paragraph_title
text: SHIPPING OPINION.

label: text
text:
The question of a harbour survey being a topical one in view of yesterday's Council discussions and the assurance given by the Government, a "China Mail" representative made enquiries this morning as to the opinion in local shipping circles on the general question of harbour dredging.
A local resident with considerable shipping interests who was approached on the matter said that to him it seemed rather extraordinary in a port of such magnitude and importance as Hongkong, situated as it was at the mouth of a river, that the local Government had not a dredger of its own.

label: text
text: In the opinion of the gentleman in question there was bound to be silting in a port such as this and in spite of the assurance given in Council he was convinced that silting had had an effect on the shoal upon which two ships had recently grounded.

label: text
text: Hiring Difficulties.

label: text
text: Questioned as to the expense involved in the construction of a dredger, our informant said this would undoubtedly be very heavy but he did not see how else the situation was to be met. The question had been raised as to the possible use of the Netherlands Harbour Works dredger at Macao which he believed was the second largest dredger in the world. This had been of great use in the dredging operations prior to the construction of the quay wall at North Point but what assurance had the Government if it wanted to carry out dredging in five years that this dredger would be available then? It was only here at present because of its use in the Macao Harport works construction.

label: text
text: Another shipping man approached by the reporter said that the only alternative to the construction of a dredger or the hire of one was the rudimentary operation carried out by hand such as one observed in Chinese waters near Canton. This, of course, would be absurd to apply to a port like Hongkong.

label: text
text: From further enquiries it would appear that the Government dredger "St. Enoch" was abandoned on account of the expense of upkeep. Residents of many years' standing remember it sinking in the Harbour off the Hongkong Club and H.M.S. "Powerful," then in the harbour, assisting in the salving. The Hongkong and Whampoa Dock Company dredger was used in connection with certain works up to 1912 when it was sold for the purpose of dredging.

label: text
text: So it would appear that, for some years (until the Netherlands Harbour Works dredger was sent to Macao) there was not, even a dredger in the Far East which could be hired if dredging in the harbour had proved imperative.

label: text
text: He recalled the story that it took the Bishop with the broken leg, to see that the broken bridge was mended.

label: text
text: Mr. Bird spoke of boulders coming down the nullahs. Of course they did. They came down and the bridges not being wide enough to pass them the nullahs were blocked.

label: text
text: He remembered two years ago when at Magazine Gap Road the same thing occurred. The bridge was blocked by boulders and the water swept down and washed the road and the bridge. They had only to go this year to Kennedy Road and Macdonnell Road to see what he had seen and reason how it all came about. If the nuliahs were properly looked after or perhaps diverted—they could undoubtedly be rendered safe when filled with storm water.

label: text

BATTLE BETWEEN AEROPLANE
VESSEL

label: text
text: A SHOWER OF BOMBS.

label: text
text: A battle between a Government bombing aeroplane and a gun-running vessel endeavouring to land arms for the revolutionary forces is described in a report from Managua.

label: text
text:
Two former American aviators, who are now employed with the Nicaraguan Constabulary, located a vessel off Corinto. Dropping to a low altitude they discharged a shower of bombs on the vessel, which went out to sea, the crew machine-gunning the aeroplane, which pursued her till its bombs ran out. On the same night the aeroplane, having been replenished, returned and dropped more bombs, but darkness ended the fight.

Reuter.
